case_name: Manish Sisodia v. Central Bureau of Investigation

pages.text:
REPORTABLE
IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CRIMINAL APPEAL NO. 3387 OF 2023

MANISH SISODIA ... APPELLANT
VERSUS
CENTRAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION ... RESPONDENT

JUDGMENT

SANJIV KHANNA, J.

1. The appellant seeks regular bail under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (CrPC) in cases investigated by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and Directorate of Enforcement (ED) concerning the Delhi Excise Policy.

2. Right to speedy trial is a fundamental right under Article 21 of the Constitution of India. In cases where the trial gets delayed and incarceration extends beyond a reasonable period, the constitutional court is empowered to grant bail even in matters involving stringent statutory conditions.

3. Prolonged pre-trial detention without commencement or conclusion of trial cannot become punitive. If the trial cannot proceed with reasonable dispatch, the accused is entitled to renew the prayer for bail under Section 439 CrPC.
